title: Book One · Chapter 74: The Heavy Little Cup
story:
Ronan puts the first thing in the water. It is not a boat.

It is a little ball of clay. He rolls it between his hands. Soon it is round and smooth. Leo laughs. “It looks like a grey dumpling.”

“Do not eat it,” Miss Wu tells him.

“I was not going to.”

“You looked interested.”

She sets the basin on a low table. There is a cloth under it. Four children may stand round it at one time. The others must watch from their seats.

Ronan puts the ball in. It falls straight to the bottom.

“That sinks,” he says.

Mei draws a small circle at the bottom of her picture.

Leo made his clay long and thin. It sinks too, but one end touches the bottom first.

“Mine went more slowly,” he says.

“Did we measure the time?” Miss Wu asks.

“No.”

“We watched the test. Now write the result.”

Leo writes: The long one went down with its nose first. Ronan likes the word nose for a piece of clay.

Mei presses her clay into a small cup. She makes the bottom wide. The sides are uneven. One is much higher than the other.

“That is not a boat,” Ronan says.

“I made a cup.”

She puts it on the water. It stays there.

Ronan bends closer. The grey clay is still clay. Mei used the same clay to make her cup. But the ball sank, and this cup floats.

Then water comes over the low side. The cup slowly leans and drops.

“It sank,” Leo says.

“It floated first,” Mei says.

Miss Wu gives her a dry cloth. “You need both things on your page.”

Ronan takes his ball from the basin. He presses his thumb into it. The clay feels cold and wet. His first cup has a hole in the bottom. He closes the hole, but then one side tears.

Leo wants another turn at the basin. Ronan keeps pressing.

“Let him put his in while you work,” Mei says.

Ronan moves aside. He feels cross for a moment. But Mei is right about the space.

His next cup floats for a short time. He holds his breath and watches the low side. He hopes no water will come over it. One side folds inward. The little cup fills.

He writes: It floats. Then he looks at the basin and adds: Then it sinks.

Miss Wu comes past. She does not put a cross beside his words.

“Do you want a clean page?” she asks.

“Is this wrong?”

“No. It is rather wet.”

There are five grey finger marks by his drawing. He keeps the page anyway. He remembers the hole in his first cup. He closed that hole. He wants to remember that step.

At the end, Miss Wu keeps the clay for later. She lets them press the wet pieces together. Ronan finds his old round ball inside his broken cup. He rolls the whole piece gently between his hands again. It is nearly the same size as before. Ronan wants to try more shapes next time. Now he knows some shapes float longer than others. He leaves a thumb mark in the top. That will help him find his piece next time.

They wash their hands. Then they line up for the next lesson. Leo whispers, “My clay boat needs a captain.”

“Not you,” Mei says. “You would tip it over.”

“So would you.”

“A clay captain,” Ronan says.

They each hold up a thumb. They pretend their thumbs are little captains. Miss Wu looks at the three thumbs. She asks the captains to face the front too.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- clay＝黏土
- uneven＝不平整的
- tip it over＝把它弄翻
- at one time＝同时

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：dumpling＝饺子；thumb＝拇指；captain＝船长。

## 读句提示

**I made a cup.**

我／做了／一个杯子。不需要用what I made来指这个杯子。

## 理解问题

1. Mei的黏土小杯经历了哪两个不同结果？
2. Ronan为什么保留带灰手印的纸？
